headline: Apple opens Siri to competing AI models, fragmenting voice assistant landscape
body: Apple's latest code reveals that Siri can now be swapped out for alternative AI models like Claude and ChatGPT, signaling a fundamental shift toward modular voice assistant architecture. This modularity matters for healthcare organizations because clinical voice workflows currently depend on tightly integrated AI systems from single vendors, and provider choice could reshape EHR dictation, clinical documentation, and bedside interaction standards. Health systems may soon face decisions about which underlying LLM to deploy for patient-facing and clinician-facing voice interfaces, introducing new considerations around model performance, compliance, and data residency. The fragmentation also complicates vendor lock-in dynamics that currently favor integrated suites, potentially creating opportunities for healthcare AI consultants to architect custom voice pipelines tailored to specific clinical workflows rather than accepting default implementations.
